CLAUDE.md — sharedimp (R)

Source: CLAUDE.md

What this package is

sharedimp implements the linear-regression variant of Ultra-marginal Feature Importance (UMFI-LR, Janssen, Guan & Robeva, AISTATS 2023) as a careful, resampling-based R package built on tidymodels (parsnip / rsample / yardstick). It is a companion to the Python package in ../sharedimp-py; both follow docs/specification.md (v0.1, reconciled 2026-11-13), which is the single source of truth for the algorithm, inputs, outputs and metric conventions. The goal is that R and Python compute the same UMFI-LR quantity; paper benchmarks live in ../sharedimp-experiments, not here. Never edit files in the sibling repositories from this one; report differences instead (docs/python_changes.md lists what Python still has to change).

We do not claim a new importance measure. Do not describe the output as a causal or conditional effect. Do not add confidence intervals, p-values, or other formal inference. Keep the user-facing API small: shared_importance() plus a few accessors and low-level helpers.

Algorithm (summary; details in docs/specification.md)

For each split and each anchor feature i:

  1. On the training rows only, regress every other feature X_j on X_i (OLS with intercept) and keep (a_j, b_j).
  2. Residualize training and assessment rows with the same coefficients: R_j = X_j − a_j − b_j X_i. A column that is an exact affine function of the anchor on the training rows (SS_res <= 1e-10 SS_tot) gets a residual of exactly 0 and is kept. A constant anchor (max == min, exact) gets slopes 0 and a warning; a constant other column gets slope 0 and its value as intercept.
  3. Full representation = X with the other columns replaced by their residuals, the anchor raw and in its original position; reduced representation = full without the anchor column. Column count is always p and p − 1; nothing is dropped.
  4. Fit the learner on both representations, predict the assessment rows, evaluate the metric on each.
  5. Scores are oriented greater-is-better (score = metric for maximize metrics, −metric for minimize metrics); importance = score_full − score_reduced, so positive always means “keeping the anchor helps”. Negatives are kept.
  6. Aggregate by the mean over splits; report split-level results too.

Defaults: 5-fold CV (stratified for classification), random forest via ranger with 500 trees / min_n = 5, MSE for regression and log loss for classification. p = 1 is allowed: the reduced model is the null model.

Output schema (shared with Python)

  • $importance: feature, importance, importance_std, score_full, score_reduced, n_splits — one row per anchor in features order.
  • fold_results(): feature, split, n_train, n_test, score_full, score_reduced, importance (common) + id, id2, error (R only) — ordered by split, then feature.

The direction diagnostic is not part of the v0.1 API (the R and Python drafts defined different statistics). R/direction.R is kept internal and unexported; do not expose it without an agreed definition.

Code layout

  • R/residualize.R — pure matrix core: residualize_fit(), residualize_apply(), build_representations(). No learner or tidymodels code here.
  • R/learners.R — learner adapters: sharedimp_learner(), built-in "linear" (lm.fit / glm.fit / nnet::multinom, aliased coefficients → 0) and "rand_forest", parsnip model_spec adapter, null model.
  • R/metrics.R — metric adapters around yardstick; direction handling; mse.
  • R/shared_importance.R — orchestration (splits × anchors), seeding, errors.
  • R/result.R — sharedimp_result class, print(), fold_results().
  • R/direction.R — experimental, unexported, unreachable from the API.
  • tests/testthat/ — one file per concern; see “Testing”.
  • docs/STATUS.md — running work log and TODO list across the three repos; read it first when resuming, update it at the end of a session.
  • docs/specification.md — common spec. docs/python_changes.md — what the Python side must change. docs/parity/ — cross-language verification record. docs/umfi_comparison.md — comparison with the reference implementation.

Citation

CITATION.cff (Rbuildignored) holds the citation metadata: author from DESCRIPTION, the UMFI paper as preferred-citation, the Python package under references. Only verified facts go in it: no affiliation or ORCID has been confirmed, and no DOI for the (unsubmitted) SoftwareX paper. Add the DOI only once the paper is published.

Development environment

R is not on the PATH on this machine. Use the conda environment:

R=/home/koki/anaconda3/envs/sharedimp-dev/bin/Rscript
$R -e 'devtools::document()'
$R -e 'devtools::test()'
$R -e 'devtools::check()'          # full R CMD check
$R -e 'devtools::build_vignettes()'

Run devtools::document() after changing roxygen comments; NAMESPACE and man/ are generated, do not hand-edit them. The Python package can be run for comparisons from ../sharedimp-py with its .venv/bin/python (read-only; never edit that repository from here).

Docker image

Dockerfile (base rocker/r-ver:<R_VERSION>, pinned stable R; not Bioconductor, which sharedimp does not need) installs the Imports plus nnet, testthat, withr, installs the package with --install-tests, runs tools::testInstalledPackage() and docker/smoke-test.R during the build, and removes the sources. .dockerignore keeps docs, CI files and build artifacts out of the context; Dockerfile, .dockerignore and docker/ are in .Rbuildignore.

.github/workflows/build_test_push.yml (policy from dsc-chiba-u/fbrglm with refinements): pull requests build and test only; pushes to main publish the same build to ghcr.io/dsc-chiba-u/sharedimp-r and koki/sharedimp-r with tags latest + short SHA via docker/metadata-action and one docker/build-push-action call; vX.Y.Z tags publish semver tags without latest; missing DOCKER_USERNAME / DOCKER_PASSWORD secrets fail the publishing run early with an explicit message; GHCR uses GITHUB_TOKEN. A manual run with publish=false (gh workflow run build_test_push.yml -f publish=false) builds and tests only, which validates the Dockerfile in CI without registry credentials. Docker is not usable from the sandbox on this machine (snap socket owned by root), so verify image changes through the Actions run, or run sudo docker build . yourself. Never report a registry push as successful without seeing the workflow succeed.

Constraints

  • Numeric predictors only; no imputation; factors in x are an error.
  • Residualization coefficients must be estimated on the training rows only. Any change touching build_representations() must keep the leakage tests and the cross-language fixture (test-common-spec.R) passing.
  • Fixed hyperparameters inside shared_importance(); no tuning.
  • Negative importance is never truncated.
  • Metric direction is taken from the yardstick direction attribute; never hard-code a sign for a named metric elsewhere. r2 means rsq_trad (1 − SS_res/SS_tot), rsq means squared Pearson correlation; keep them distinct.
  • Learner failures on a split produce NA for that split plus a warning, not an abort (unless on_error = "error").
  • Dependencies: Imports are parsnip, rsample, yardstick, ranger, rlang, tibble, stats. Everything else (glmnet, kernlab, ggplot2, nnet, …) is Suggests and must be guarded with requireNamespace().
  • Target CRAN quality: R CMD check with no ERRORs/WARNINGs; examples run in seconds; tests deterministic (always pass seed or explicit resamples).

Testing policy

Start from tiny deterministic synthetic data and verify against hand computation before testing behaviour statistically.

  1. Residualization coefficients equal lm(X_j ~ X_i) on the training rows.
  2. Training and assessment rows are transformed with the same coefficients.
  3. Assessment rows do not influence the coefficients (perturbing assessment rows leaves training representations unchanged).
  4. Full / reduced representations have the specified columns and order (anchor in place); importance is invariant to the column order of x.
  5. With the linear learner and MSE, importance matches the analytic expectation on a linear-Gaussian design.
  6. Exact duplicates (zero residual column, kept), independent predictors and p = 1 (null model) behave as specified.
  7. Comparison with the reference UMFI-LR preprocessing (function re-implemented in the test) — document, never fabricate, agreement.
  8. Smoke tests for regression / binary / multiclass with both built-in learners and a parsnip spec.
  9. Negative importance survives; learner failures yield NA + warning.
  10. Output schema (both tables) and the deterministic cross-language fixture of specification Section 15.1 reproduce the recorded values; metric definitions match the specification table.

Use custom learners that record the matrices they receive to test the pipeline without depending on a particular model.

Commit discipline

Small, focused commits with imperative messages. Run devtools::test() before committing; run devtools::check() before pushing anything that changes DESCRIPTION, NAMESPACE, or exported functions. Never report a test or check as passing without having run it.
